reason: Reads Turtle with a blank-node activity or mention subject and finds each association or mention with the blank node as its first party, the expected other parties and no ProvWarning besides the not-converted warning. Issue #674 and section 3.2 of planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md, which reads a blank-node subject's qualification node and prov:asInBundle bundle as an IRI subject's.

Turtle with a literal typed <urn:example:t=> raises ProvRDFException whose message says Cannot split IRI 'urn:example:t='. docs/reference/serializers.md (exception tree) makes ProvRDFException the error for a failure to read PROV-O. Took over the job of the removed test_rdf.py::test_unsplittable_iri_raises_clear_error. It reaches the same raise in `ProvRDFSerializer._split_at_separator` through `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri` and the URIRef arm of `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_rdf_representation`, which `ProvRDFSerializer._decode_literal_representation` calls for the datatype, and its match= holds the check of the IRI in the message. The verifier's faults that dropped the IRI from the message and that raised ValueError in place of ProvRDFException failed this test and test_exceptions.py::test_a_typed_subject_with_no_separator_raises_the_rdf_error. A fault that swallowed the exception in `ProvRDFSerializer._decode_literal_representation` failed this test alone of the two, because the removed test's direct call skips that caller.

A Literal typed with a datatype whose local part is c:d, under the default namespace or under an unbound prefix zz, round trips through Turtle to an equal document. #665 (the PROV-O reader dropped a datatype whose IRI it cannot compact).

A document with the prov:Location value maybe typed xsd:boolean writes Turtle that holds prov:atLocation "maybe"^^xsd:boolean. #575 (the PROV-O writer rewrote an ill-formed xsd:boolean) and docs/reference/conformance.md C10 (rdflib rewrites some literal texts when it parses, so the writer keeps the text it was given).

Turtle with the short IRI http://alice.example, as a foaf:homepage object or an ex:site object, reads with ex, ns1 and every rdflib http binding registered and the foaf attribute names under the foaf prefix. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) says a namespace minted for a short IRI declares every rdflib default binding under it, and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md decision N56 rules that those bindings register before the minted namespace.

Round-trips a document with one relation through PROV-O and finds one record before and after and an equal document. The 13 rows are anonymous-extra-<family> for usage, communication, attribution, influence and delegation with an extra attribute, which #303 fixed because they decoded into two records, identified-extra-<family> for the four identified relations, which were never affected and guard against a regression, and anonymous-bare-<family> for the four anonymous relations with no extra attribute, which are only written as the binary triple. Renamed from test_anonymous_qualified_relation_with_extra_attributes_round_trips, and it gained the rows of test_identified_qualified_relation_with_extra_attributes_round_trips and test_anonymous_qualified_relation_without_extra_attributes_round_trips. The three bodies were the same, so no row gains or changes an assertion. Every lambda carries over, each group keeps its comment, and the verifier found each row's arcs identical to its original. The round trip passes through `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_document` and `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_document`. Nothing is lost, and the ids still name the shape of a failing case.

Writes an entity whose prov:type is the text of a PROV class IRI (Generation or Activity), reads it back with the rdf:type triples met in each order and finds a document equal to the original. The refusal of an IRI typed as an element and a relation (issue #743) must not apply to a string value, which prov 3.2.3 read back as the entity's prov:type.

Passes the rdf:type triples of two PROV classes, in each order, to ProvRDFSerializer._register_record_type and finds it reports a prov:type only for the subclass, or for a class that is no base of the record type. Caveat C12 on docs/reference/conformance.md says a subject typed with a record type's class and a subclass of it reads back with the subclass as a prov:type, in every triple order.

Serialises alternate(ex:alt1, ex:alt2) as N-Triples 1.1 and finds alt1 as the subject of prov:alternateOf and alt1 before alt2 in the output. Issue #258 and the Component 5 text of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says alternate(a, b) is written as the triple a prov:alternateOf b.

Writes an identified alternate as N-Triples 1.1 with a ProvWarning that names the dropped identifier and finds the written text reads back as the alternate without it. Issue #759 and the Component 5 text of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says the PROV-O writer drops an alternate's identifier with a ProvWarning.

Writes an identified derivation whose prov:type values are prov:Derivation and a subtype in either order (or a subtype alone) and finds exactly those classes as rdf:type of the derivation's IRI in the encoded graph. Issue #697, the PROV-O writer's rdf:type prov:Derivation depending on attribute order, and caveat C12 on docs/reference/conformance.md.

Round-trips an entity whose prov:type is prov:Entity through PROV-O and finds the reloaded entity with no prov:type and unequal to the original. Caveat C12 on docs/reference/conformance.md says a prov:type equal to the record's own class does not survive a PROV-O round trip.

Serialises two anonymous attributions of one entity to different agents with extra attributes as TriG and finds two prov:Attribution nodes, each with its own prov:agent. Issue #250, anonymous qualified nodes that omit their influencer property.

Serialises an anonymous communication, attribution, delegation or influence with an extra attribute as N-Triples 1.1 and finds the influencer predicate (prov:activity, prov:agent or prov:influencer) in the output. Issue #250, anonymous qualified nodes that omit their influencer property, and the qualification tables of the PROV-O recommendation.

Removed, folded into test_rdf.py::test_a_qualified_relation_round_trips_as_one_record as the four rows anonymous-bare-<family> (#303, whose fix applies to qualified nodes only, so these rows guard the binary-triple form against a regression). The lambdas, the one-record checks before and after, the equality check and the comment carry over, and the verifier found each row's arcs identical to its original.

Round-trips two usages and a generation with extra attributes and no identifier under a default namespace and finds three records with no identifier and an equal document. Issue #525 and the PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says a relation whose subject is a blank node reads with no identifier.

A Turtle value aGVsbG8= typed xsd:base64Binary on an entity reads as the Literal aGVsbG8= of that datatype, not as a bytes repr. #288 (a base64Binary literal read from PROV-O gave the bytes repr) and docs/reference/conformance.md (Literals table) says an xsd:base64Binary literal keeps its lexical form and datatype as given.

Reads Turtle whose derivation has a prov:hadGeneration or prov:hadUsage pointing at a blank node, typed or untyped, and finds one ProvWarning naming the dropped attribute and a derivation without that value. Issue #639 and the PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says an attribute whose object is a blank node that names no record is dropped with a ProvWarning.

Reads Turtle with an association whose prov:hadPlan is a blank-node element, placed before or after the association, and finds ProvRDFException whose cause is ProvElementIdentifierRequired and whose message is the subject plus that cause. #639 and the PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md say a blank node that is an element's subject resolves as that element's identifier does. Proposed as the target of a merge with test_rdf.py::test_blank_node_element_still_takes_its_label_as_identifier and kept apart. The judge found two behaviours with two raise sites and two bullets of that section, so the merge would mix behaviours that keep their own names. Reads Turtle with an extra attribute whose object is a blank node and finds a ProvWarning naming the attribute and an entity without that value. Issue #639 and the PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says such an attribute is dropped with a ProvWarning.

Reads Turtle with a blank-node entity and no default namespace and finds ProvRDFException whose cause is ProvElementIdentifierRequired and whose message is the subject plus that cause. The PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md says an element's blank-node label resolves in the default namespace. Proposed for a merge into test_rdf.py::test_blank_node_behind_an_element_is_the_elements_own_problem and kept apart. The two tests pin two behaviours that keep their own names, with two raise sites and two bullets of that section. The merge would also rename test_rdf.py::test_blank_node_behind_an_element_is_the_elements_own_problem, one of the #639 tests named alike beside test_rdf.py::test_blank_node_behind_a_relation_is_dropped. The classifier cited #525, which is about record equality and is not this test's source.

Reads Turtle with a membership whose prov:entity is a blank node and finds two ProvWarning messages (the dropped attribute, then the skipped statement), no other ProvWarning and no records. Issue #639 and section 4.6 of planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md (issue #710), which makes the PROV-O reader warn and skip a membership missing its entity.

A prefix bl registered only on a bundle appears as @prefix bl in the TriG output, and no ns1 prefix appears. #96 (namespace prefixes missing from the RDF output), which HISTORY.md lists as an improvement for bundle-local prefixes.

When a bundle registers the prefix coll for an IRI other than the document's coll, the TriG output declares @prefix coll only for the document IRI and declares the bundle IRI as coll1. #96 (namespace prefixes missing from the RDF output), which HISTORY.md lists as an improvement for bundle-local prefixes.

Five namespaces registered on a bundle are bound on the bundle's PROV-O graph in registration order. #337 (namespace declaration order depended on PYTHONHASHSEED), and HISTORY.md says the PROV-XML and PROV-O writers declare a bundle's namespaces in registration order.

Round-trips a document with an entity, an activity, a generation and an attribution under a default namespace through TriG with the not-converted warning turned into an error and finds an equal document. The PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says one ProvWarning lists the subjects that get no record of their own.

Removed, folded into test_rdf.py::test_decode_unrelated_provexception_is_not_relabelled_as_scruffy as the row agreeing-values (#217). Reads Turtle with the triple ex:e1 prov:alternateOf ex:e2 and finds one alternate whose formal attributes are ex:e1 then ex:e2. Issue #258 and the Component 5 text of docs/reference/conformance.md, which gives PROV-DM's argument order for alternate.

Calls ProvRDFSerializer.decode_document on a Dataset whose named graph IRI matches no registered namespace and finds one bundle with that IRI holding one record. The PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md says a syntax with named graphs, such as TriG, keeps each bundle as a separate graph.

Removed. Calling `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_document` with a plain rdflib Graph that holds one prov:Entity triple found one record. It was added to close a coverage gap and names no issue or document. No public read reaches the plain-Graph arm of `ProvRDFSerializer._decode_graphs`, because every read passes a Dataset (the verifier's probe), and no page under docs/reference/ renders ProvRDFSerializer. test_rdf.py::test_the_graph_lookup_snapshot_lasts_one_decode (row colon-less-iri, #691) takes over. The comment in this test said every other test parses into a Dataset, which stopped being true when the colon-less helper began passing a plain Graph.

Reads Turtle with two prov:startedAtTime values on one qualified prov:Start node and finds ProvRDFException with the documented-limitation message and a ProvException cause. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md and issues #217 and #299.

Removed, folded into test_rdf.py::test_decode_qualified_time_predicate_lands_in_formal_time as the row end (#299, the End half of the fix). Writes an identified start with a time, finds prov:atTime and no startedAtTime in the PROV-O text, reads it back and finds the time in the formal time slot. Issue #299, which moved prov:startedAtTime into the formal time slot and left the prov:atTime spelling that prov writes unchanged.

Reads Turtle with a qualified prov:Start or prov:End node that carries prov:startedAtTime or prov:endedAtTime, and finds the time in the record's formal time slot and no prov:startTime or prov:endTime extra attribute (#299). Renamed from test_decode_qualified_start_started_at_time_lands_in_formal_time, which is the row start, and it gained the row end from test_decode_qualified_end_ended_at_time_lands_in_formal_time. Reads eight Turtle documents that type one subject with a base class and its subclass, two element classes, a non-prov qualification predicate or a prov-written subclass type, and finds the expected records and no exception. Caveat C12 on docs/reference/conformance.md and the ruling L17 in planning/specs/2026-11-02-release-3.3.0-spec7-loose-ends-freeze.md (issue #743), which refuses only an element beside a relation.

Writes a usage and a generation that share one identifier, reads the PROV-O text back and finds no exception. The ruling L17 in planning/specs/2026-11-02-release-3.3.0-spec7-loose-ends-freeze.md (issue #743) leaves two relations on one IRI unchanged beside the new element-and-relation refusal.

Reads Turtle in which one IRI is typed as an element class and a relation class, in either order the reader meets them, or a qualification node is typed only as an element, and finds ProvRDFException with the one-sentence message and no cause. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md covers an identifier that names an element and a relation, and issue #743 and the ruling L17 in planning/specs/2026-11-02-release-3.3.0-spec7-loose-ends-freeze.md fix the refusal.

Reads Turtle whose reader order puts the qualifier's prov:activity last and finds ProvRDFException with the documented-limitation message, so neither value is dropped. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md and issue #217.

Reads six Turtle documents in which an identified or blank relation node repeats a formal attribute and finds ProvRDFException with the documented-limitation message and the model's exception as its cause. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md and issue #217.

Writes two usages that share an identifier and differ in their entity, reads the PROV-O text back and finds ProvRDFException with the documented-limitation message. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md and issue #217.

Writes two generations, usages, starts, ends or invalidations that share an identifier and differ in time, reads the PROV-O text back and finds ProvRDFException with the documented-limitation message. Caveat C1 on docs/reference/conformance.md and issue #217.

Reads Turtle that repeats no formal attribute with differing values, and finds ProvRDFException naming the subject, with ProvExceptionInvalidQualifiedName as its cause and neither the documented-limitation text nor conformance.md in the message. #217 and caveat C1 of docs/reference/conformance.md limit that message to a repeated formal attribute. The row single-values has one prov:activity triple whose object is a plain literal. The row agreeing-values is a usage that repeats its activity in prov:activity beside an invalid prov:entity, folded in from test_decode_agreeing_values_are_not_relabelled_as_scruffy. A Turtle round trip of an entity holding an xsd:gYear 2020, an xsd:gYearMonth 2020-05 and an xsd:QName ex:e1 reads the first two with the texts 2020 and 2020-05 and the third as the qualified name ex:e1. docs/reference/conformance.md (Literals table) says the other XSD types keep their lexical form and datatype as given, and an xsd:QName literal whose prefix is declared is a qualified name.

A Turtle document whose entity has an rdfs:label of U+2019 typed xsd:string reads with that character in its prov:label value. docs/reference/conformance.md (Literals table) says a string, with or without an explicit xsd:string, reads in every format.

A document with the default namespace http://default.example/ writes Turtle that declares @prefix : for it and writes the entity as :e1. #96 (namespace prefixes missing from the RDF output), which HISTORY.md lists as an improvement for the default namespace.

Calls `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_container` on a one-entity document, once with no container (the graph uses rdflib's default store type and has a prov binding) and once with a Dataset container (the same object comes back holding triples). No page under docs/reference/ renders ProvRDFSerializer or this method. Public serialisation never reaches the no-container branch, because `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_document` always passes its own Graph, and the verifier's probe over nine rdf formats, read and auto-detection saw only Graph containers. The no-container branch is reached through `prov.serializers.get("rdf")` alone. `test_rdf.py::test_bundle_namespace_order_follows_registration_in_rdf` also calls `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_container` with no container. The judge's fault that ignores the caller's container in `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_container` failed 14 other tests through `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_document`, but each passes a plain Graph, so none takes over the Dataset case. The prov binding assertion passes with the `nm.bind("prov", PROV.uri)` line removed from `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_container`, because a new Graph already binds prov at rdflib 7.1.1 and 7.6.0, and the whole suite passed with that line removed. Ruled query by the maintainer, who left the test in place until a contract for the method is named, or until the test and its code go together. Later audit: the section that checks a call with no container, verdict rewrite.

Calls the module's find_diff helper on two graphs that differ by one triple, on two of two triples and on identical graphs, and finds a mismatch, a mismatch and a match. Issue #304, find_diff blind to single-triple differences.

A document holding the float32-narrowed 0.1 on an entity round trips through PROV-O to an equal document. #225 (PROV-O lost the precision of a float) and docs/reference/values.md (a float is written as xsd:double with its repr).

A float subclass holding 0.1 is written to N-Triples as "0.1" typed xsd:double. docs/reference/values.md says a subclass of a listed type counts as that type and a float is written as xsd:double with its repr. Proposed for deletion and kept. This is the only test that pins the written spelling of a finite float in PROV-O output. The verifier's fault in the xsd:double branch of `ProvRDFSerializer.encode_rdf_representation`, which formats a finite value as f"{float(text):.17g}", is plausible, because `.17g` is a standard way to guarantee a float round trip. It passed the whole suite with this test deselected (5302 passed) and failed this test, under hash seeds 1 to 8 and rdflib 7.1.1. The reader repairs the spelling, so the proposed takeover `test_literal_semantics.py::test_a_subclass_of_a_plain_type_is_written_as_the_plain_value` (row float-rdf) passes under it.

Removed, folded into test_rdf.py::test_a_qualified_relation_round_trips_as_one_record as the four rows identified-extra-<family> (#303, whose fix left identified relations unaffected, so these rows guard against a regression). An xsd:gYear Literal with the text year and an xsd:gYearMonth Literal with the text month each round trip through Turtle to an equal document. #522 (an ill-formed typed literal stays a Literal in every reader) and docs/reference/conformance.md (Literals table) says the other XSD types keep their lexical form and datatype as given.

For each of the seven PROV-N metacharacters, entities whose local part holds it inside the name or at its start round trip through PROV-O with their full IRIs. docs/reference/conformance.md C4 admits every character that PN_LOCAL can express in a local part, and #294 fixed the trailing position of the same names.

Serialises each PROV-JSON fixture to Turtle or TriG, compares its graph with the stored file in the rdf fixture folder through find_diff, apart from the skipped indexes, and reads the written text back. The Turtle and TriG files in src/prov/tests/rdf are the vendored PROV-O counterparts of the PROV-JSON files in src/prov/tests/json, and docs/development.md says per-format modules keep what is specific to the format.

Reads TriG in the form prov 2.x wrote, with two anonymous qualified delegations that have no prov:agent, and finds two delegations, one with no responsible agent and the shared delegate and activity on both. Compatibility with documents that prov 2.x and earlier wrote, which carry no influencer on an anonymous qualified node (issues #250 and #226).

Removed. Calling `literal_rdf_representation` on the Literal aGVsbG8= typed xsd:base64Binary gave an rdflib literal with the text aGVsbG8= (#288 and the Literals table of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says the lexical form and datatype stay as given). test_attributes.py::test_entity_with_one_type_attribute (row rdf-attr-28) takes over. For maybe typed xsd:boolean, 05 typed xsd:int, 1e0 typed xsd:double and PT0S typed xsd:duration, `literal_rdf_representation` and the N-Triples and default output of a document that holds the Literal keep the text as given with its datatype. #575 (the PROV-O writer rewrote an ill-formed xsd:boolean) and docs/reference/conformance.md C10 (rdflib rewrites some literal texts when it parses, so the writer keeps the text it was given). Calling `literal_rdf_representation` on a Literal with neither a datatype nor a language tag raises ValueError. No document names the raise, and no page under docs/reference/ renders the function, so its Raises docstring is no contract. No public route reaches the raise. The verifier's probe wrapped the function and tried entity and add_attributes, five attribute names, an activity and an attribution, serialize and deserialize in five formats, JSON read with and without xsd:string, unified, deepcopy and a Literal subclass, and recorded no call with neither a datatype nor a tag, because `ProvRecord._auto_literal_conversion` stores such a Literal as its text. Only a write to the private attribute store reaches the raise. Ruled query by the maintainer, who left the test in place until a contract for the raise is named, or until the test and the guard go together.

A document with the prefix nidm_groupName bound to http://purl.org/nidash/nidm#NIDM_0000170 writes Turtle that declares @prefix nidm_groupName and holds no ns1 prefix. #96 (namespace prefixes missing from the Turtle output), which HISTORY.md lists as an improvement.

Documents whose attribute keys end in : or = under a namespace used nowhere else, or whose element ids hold a colon or a quote, round trip through PROV-O to an equal document. #341 (a qualified name with a colon in its local part did not round trip through PROV-O).

TriG with @prefix : bound to http://ex.org/ and a named graph : reads as a bundle whose identifier is http://ex.org/. planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md decision N22 rejects an IRI equal to the default namespace in the model, and the amendment of 2026-10-25 gives the PROV-O reader no rejection row, so the reader keeps the IRI.

For RDF/XML, N-Triples and N-Quads, a document holding an infinity, a negative infinity and a NaN is written with INF, -INF and NaN, holds no inf or nan, and reads back the same three floats. #550 (non-finite doubles were written as inf, -inf and nan, outside the XSD lexical space) and docs/reference/values.md (a float is written as NaN, INF or -INF).

Turtle with @prefix : bound to http://ex.org/ and an attribute object : reads with an attribute value whose IRI is http://ex.org/. planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md decision N22 rejects an IRI equal to the default namespace in the model, and the amendment of 2026-10-25 gives the PROV-O reader no rejection row, so the reader keeps the IRI.

A document with the plain int 123456789000 on an entity writes N-Triples that type it xsd:long and hold no xsd:int datatype. #256 (plain ints outside 32 bits were asserted as xsd:int in RDF output) and docs/reference/values.md (an int within 64 bits is xsd:long).

A Turtle predicate under a prefix o that the graph declares reads as that attribute and raises no ProvWarning. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) says only a predicate namespace declared neither in the document nor in the graph gets a minted prefix with a ProvWarning.

A Turtle predicate under http://other.org/, declared nowhere, reads as an attribute with that full IRI and raises exactly one ProvWarning that names it. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) says an attribute predicate under a namespace declared neither in the document nor in the graph gets a minted prefix with a ProvWarning, and HISTORY.md records the warning.

Round-trips two anonymous delegations that share a delegate and an activity and differ in their responsible agent, and finds an equal document. Issues #226 and #250, the collapse of anonymous qualified delegations that share a delegate and an activity.

Decoding a graph with bound namespaces through `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_container` reads an IRI under the longest bound namespace that is a proper prefix of it, and gives its URI, namespace URI, prefix and local part. Renamed from test_resolve_iri_reuses_namespace_bound_in_graph_for_metacharacter_local_part, which is the row metacharacter-local-part (#294), and it gained the rows longest-match and equal-iri-skipped from test_resolve_iri_picks_longest_matching_bound_namespace and test_resolve_iri_skips_bound_namespace_equal_to_the_iri_itself (planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md, section 9, item 29). Each row pins one clause of the one lookup in `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri_via_graph`, which `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri` calls first. The three bodies were the same call and the same four identifier assertions, which keep their form, and each row keeps its Turtle text and its comment. The verifier found each row's arcs identical to its original. Its fault that made the first match win in `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri_via_graph` failed the row longest-match and not the other two rows. Its fault that removed the `iri != uri` guard failed the row equal-iri-skipped and not the other two. Its fault that skipped the first step of `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri` failed the rows metacharacter-local-part and equal-iri-skipped, as it failed the same two tests before the merge. Nothing is lost, and no other test pinned a form that a row replaced.

Turtle with @prefix : bound to http://ex.org/ and the subject : typed prov:Entity reads as an entity whose identifier is http://ex.org/. planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md decision N22 rejects an IRI equal to the default namespace in the model, and the amendment of 2026-10-25 gives the PROV-O reader no rejection row, so the reader keeps the IRI.

A Turtle document written with a default namespace and an ex prefix reads back with that default namespace, no registered empty prefix, a PROV-N default declaration, and a PROV-N round trip equal to it. HISTORY.md (3.3.0 Fixes, #654) says the PROV-O reader registers a default binding as the document's default namespace, and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md decision N21 rules it.

For eight rdf_format names, a document writes the same bytes with and without encoding=None, and the default write raises no UserWarning. planning/specs/2026-11-02-release-3.3.0-spec7-loose-ends-freeze.md (section 3.4, ruling L14) says the PROV-O writer passes encoding utf-8 to rdflib for every RDF format, with the byte check as the guard and the four N-Triples spellings as the fallback.

A binding added between two reads, a lookup outside a decode, two bundles that share the foaf binding and colon-less IRIs under a minted namespace each resolve against the bindings held for the decode, or the live bindings outside one. planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md (section 4.4, #691) says the reader indexes the graph's bindings once per decode and reads the live bindings for any IRI the document cannot compact. Took over the job of the removed test_rdf.py::test_decode_document_without_contexts_uses_plain_graph_path. The row colon-less-iri passes a plain Graph to `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_document`, reaches the plain-Graph arm of `ProvRDFSerializer._decode_graphs` and `ProvRDFSerializer.decode_container`, and unpacks one record with its minted attribute values. The judge's fault that made that arm decode nothing failed this row and the removed test and no other test in a whole-suite run, so the row is the arm's only pin, and a change that wraps the graph of its helper in a Dataset would leave the arm unpinned with no check noticing. The fault `compute_qname(iri, generate=False)` in `ProvRDFSerializer._resolve_iri` failed the rows colon-less-iri and bundles.

Turtle that declares prov and ex, with or without an unused foaf binding, reads with only the prefix ex registered. #654 (the PROV-O reader declared rdflib's default bindings) and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) says the document declares the source's own bindings and the namespaces its names use, and keeps a source declaration identical to an rdflib default only when a name uses it.

A document with prefixes ex, foaf and an unused un, written to Turtle and read back, equals the original and registers only ex and foaf. #654 and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O), which says a prefix the source declares and no name uses is not written by Turtle, so it does not survive a round trip.

A Turtle value typed dcterms:W3CDTF reads with the dcterms prefix registered and the datatype named dcterms:W3CDTF. #654 and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O), which says the document keeps a binding that a name read from the source uses.

An N-Triples attribution to http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/Alice reads with the foaf prefix registered and the agent named foaf:Alice. #654 and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O), which says the document keeps a binding that a name read from the source uses.

A Turtle document that binds dc to http://other.example/dc# reads dc:x as that IRI, registers dc1 for the namespace and does not declare rdflib's own dc. #654 and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O), which says rdflib replaces the source's binding of a prefix it renamed, such as dc, and the reader declares no rdflib default binding.

A literal foaf:x typed xsd:QName or prov:QUALIFIED_NAME, as an ex:p value or a prov:type value, reads as the qualified name for http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/x with foaf registered. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) says the text of an xsd:QName or prov:QUALIFIED_NAME literal registers its prefix, and the Literals table says such a literal with a declared prefix is stored as a qualified name.

A document with seven entities whose local parts end in the PROV-N metacharacters writes a Turtle graph isomorphic to the graph of those seven full IRIs typed prov:Entity. #294 and HISTORY.md, which says the fix changed no serialized output.

For each of the seven PROV-N metacharacters, an entity whose local part ends in it round trips through PROV-O with the identifier's full IRI intact. #294 (a name ending in a PROV-N metacharacter raised on read), recorded in HISTORY.md.

Reads Turtle with an entity and a subject typed only ex:Custom and finds one ProvWarning, which is also a UserWarning, naming the orphan subject and not the entity. The PROV-O section of docs/reference/conformance.md, which says one ProvWarning for each document or bundle lists the subjects typed with no PROV class, and issue #827.

A Turtle subject IRI under no declared namespace reads as an entity whose identifier has that full IRI. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-O) describes the namespaces the reader mints for an IRI no binding covers.
